Kelvin Trent Tucker was born on December 20, 1959.
Kelvin Trent Tucker is an American former professional basketball player.
Trent Tucker played eleven seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA).
Trent Tucker's position was shooting guard.
Trent Tucker's height was 6 ft 5 in (1.96 m).
Trent Tucker attended the University of Minnesota from 1978 to 1982.
Trent Tucker led the University of Minnesota to a Big Ten Conference championship in his senior year.
Trent Tucker was selected by the New York Knicks with the 6th overall pick of the 1982 NBA draft.
On November 30, 1982, Trent Tucker outscored the opposing Utah Jazz 17-11 in the third quarter during his NBA debut.
Trent Tucker represented the Knicks in the first ever Three-point Shootout (1986).
During the Three-point Shootout, Trent Tucker made it to the semifinals.
During the Three-point Shootout, Trent Tucker was outpaced by Craig Hodges and eventual winner Larry Bird.
Trent Tucker played nine seasons with the New York Knicks.
Trent Tucker joined the San Antonio Spurs in 1991.
Trent Tucker played one season with the San Antonio Spurs.
Trent Tucker joined the Chicago Bulls after his one season with the San Antonio Spurs.
The Chicago Bulls won the 1993 NBA Championship.
Trent Tucker retired after that season.
Trent Tucker had tallied 6,237 career points in his NBA career.
Trent Tucker had tallied 1,532 career assists in his NBA career.
On January 15, 1990, Trent Tucker made a three-point shot with 0.1 of a second remaining against the Chicago Bulls during an NBA game.
The shot counted and the Knicks won the game.
After the game, Bulls' coach Phil Jackson vociferously complained about the shot.
The NBA immediately established a rule on January 15, 1990, stating that 0.3 needs to be on the clock for a player to get a shot off whether they make it or not.
Inside of 0.3 seconds, only a tip-in or a high lob would count.
This rule is also used in 3x3 basketball.
After retiring, Trent Tucker worked as a broadcast analyst for Minnesota Timberwolves basketball games.
Trent Tucker currently works for KFAN radio.
Trent Tucker founded the Trent Tucker Non-Profit Organization in 1998.
On April 15, 2013, Trent began his duties as Director of District Athletics for the Minneapolis, MN Public School District.
Trent Tucker resigned from his post as Director of District Athletics for the Minneapolis, MN Public School District on February 9, 2018.
